title: The hedgehog: waiting until the break is ready
outcomes: Recognises the app's hedgehog and says which break square is attacked by two White pawns (d5) and which by one (b5)
Checks whether ...b5 or ...d5 is ready: the break square's attackers and defenders, and whether a pawn can recapture
Plays a waiting or improving move when no break is ready, instead of forcing one
As the space side, sees that a quick strike (c5 or e5) must be tested before it is played

steps.text:
The app's **hedgehog**: pawns on b6, d6 and e6 and none on the c-file, against pawns on c4 and e4 and none on the d-file (colours may be reversed). This is the app's own definition.
Rule of thumb: the cramped side keeps its pieces flexible behind the sixth rank and waits for ...b5 or ...d5. The space side guards its space or strikes first.

steps.caption: Black to move. Black has waited behind the sixth rank. White's pawn on c4 attacks b5; Black's pawn on a6 can recapture there. The break is ready.

line.say: b5: the a6 pawn can recapture on b5, and the engine rates it within 0.4 pawns of its best.

claims.statement: Open files: none. Half-open for White: d. Half-open for Black: c.
One White pawn (on c4) attacks b5.
After b5 cxb5, one Black pawn (on a6) can recapture on b5.
b5 is within 0.4 pawns of the engine's best move at depth 16.
After b5 cxb5 axb5 a Black pawn stands on b5.

steps.text: **Rule of thumb, with conditions.** Waiting is a plan only while White cannot make progress. A break needs enough defenders and a pawn to recapture: ...b5 wants the pawn on a6; d5 is attacked by two pawns (c4, e4), b5 by one. Played too early, a break can lose a pawn. Counting is the first check, not the whole answer. Space has a cost too: pushed pawns leave weaknesses.

steps.title: Same break, one pawn different
steps.prompt: In the first two positions only Black's a-pawn differs (a6 or a7). Predict whether ...b5 works in each, then check. The third position is the worked example with one White pawn moved: is it still the hedgehog?

steps.text: **The space side.** White's usual plans are to keep the space and watch the breaks, or to strike first with c5 or e5. The next positions are unlabeled: decide whether a break is ready, whether Black should wait, or whether a quick strike is a good idea. Striking first is a rule of thumb, not a duty: test what c5 or e5 gives up before playing either.

steps.prompt: Think about the positions you played without hints. As the cramped side: how did you decide between waiting and breaking? As the space side: what did you check before pushing a pawn? Write one line each.
